properties.name: 106 of 108 Components read `planned` on a system that ships — the status a Component is born with was never moved, so "born planned" is also "never promoted"
properties.statement: Found sideways on 2026-09-13 while measuring how much of the concept-stage vocabulary reflow2's own design reaches (the pseudo-design brainstorm): jq over docs/design/reflow2.json at 4,380 nodes — Components with status `planned`: 106 of 108. Capabilities by contrast read realized/verified in the majority (247 total; delivery computed along the thread), and 342 Artifacts are registered with checksums, so the BUILD is recorded — it is the Component tier whose status field nobody moves. The design's own doctrine is that a status is a measurement at an instant and that delivery is computed from the thread rather than read from a status field, so this is not a delivery error; it is a record that reads confident and wrong at the Component tier (the class epoch:a-record-that-still-reads-confident names), and it is the same shape the reflow review found in reflow ("PASS - production-ready" beside "unusable"). CAUSE NOT ASSERTED: whether nothing on the surface moves Component.status, or whether the guided paths never say to, is not measured here — the root-cause skill is the step before anyone writes one. Reported as an observation; it may also be a candidate for the "a settled node with nobody's name on it" and "prose predates its status" family of checks, which look at the other tiers.
